disposition_reason: Single-author perspective proposing that molybdenum deficiency plus dietary purines could initiate Parkinson's disease; no new data, figures are secondary.
disposition_locator: Abstract (p. 1); Molybdenum deficiency section (p. 3); Guam section (p. 4)
regulatory_or_exposure: Average daily diet molybdenum content calculated from earlier surveys: 0.07 ppm (US), 0.04 ppm (UK); CNS disease in molybdenum-deficient sheep below 0.04 ppm dietary molybdenum (pp. 1, 3; secondary)
non_numeric_findings: Southern Guam garden soils mean 0.85 ppm molybdenum (range 0.1 to 1.6, n = 24) vs 4.3 ppm in one limestone soil (p. 4; secondary)
Hypothesis: low xanthine oxidase-dehydrogenase activity in molybdenum deficiency allows dietary purines to be salvaged into the CNS (pp. 1 to 2)
